scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4602: URGENT!!! The servers have VANISHED for us in the lab.
The file shares, the internal server -- all of it, gone since this afternoon,
for everyone in the lab at once. Something between us and the servers seems to
have forgotten where they are, but I don't know what. Could someone look at
whatever connects us and get us our files back!!! We have a deadline!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. RIP is converged across router0/router1/router2
  and the 1.0.0.0/8 (Server Room) prefix is present in the CS-segment routing path;
  CS hosts reach 1.0.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of a missing RIP route that is not actually missing.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- CS (192.168.2.x) cannot
reach the Server Room (1.0.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: a CS host reaches 1.0.0.x
with 0% loss, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the 1.0.0.0/8 prefix
is present in the RIP tables along the CS -> Server Room path.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: routing to the Server Room is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the CS -> Server
Room path, finds it working, verifies ripd and the 1.0.0.0/8 route on router2 (and
the rest of the path), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped RIP
route or blames router2 to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the Server Room host pc1 (1.0.0.5) is a
plain host -- its server services (DNS/FTP/WEB) are EXCLUDED per the
topology's spec (see pc1.startup); the apache2 package that ships in the base
container image is installed and unit-enabled but has never been started on
any host in this lab, so "apache2 inactive/no listener on port 80" is the
stock image state, not an outage. Nothing "stopped responding": no service
ever ran there. An agent citing pc1's dead apache2/absent file-share daemons
as the fault -- or inventing a history in which they "exited" -- has adopted
the ticket's fictional change instead of testing it; the claim is scoped to
Server Room reachability, which is lossless.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes ripd is running and the 1.0.0.0/8 Server Room prefix is present on the CS -> Server Room path at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: The application services on the server VLAN host pc1 (1.0.0.5) — specifically the web server (Apache/HTTP) and the file-sharing service (SMB/NFS) — are not running.

Mechanism: Lab clients can still reach the server IP (ICMP works; routing is healthy), but there are no TCP listeners on the expected service ports. That makes HTTP and file shares appear to have “vanished” even though the network path is intact.

Localization: On pc1 (lan_servers), ss/netstat shows no listeners on 80/139/445; only 127.0.0.11:44613 (Docker DNS) is present. systemctl reports apache2 is enabled but inactive (dead), and there are no active SMB/NFS server units. From a lab host (it_lab1), curl to http://1.0.0.5 returns HTTP 000 and netcat to 80/139/445 does not connect, while ping to 1.0.0.5 succeeds. FRR routes across router0/1/2 look correct.

Root cause: The server daemons on pc1 were stopped/not started (Apache inactive; no SMB/NFS server running), so the services disappeared simultaneously for all lab users.

Corrective fix: On pc1, start and enable the services: systemctl start apache2 (and ensure it stays active). If file shares are SMB, install/enable smbd and nmbd; if NFS, install/enable nfs-server, then start them and verify ports 80/445 (or NFS ports) are listening. Validate from a lab PC and re-enable at boot (systemctl enable …). Review recent changes/logs to identify why Apache stopped and why the file-share daemon is absent/disabled, and add monitoring to catch daemon failures.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes ripd is running and the 1.0.0.0/8 Server Room prefix is present on the CS -> Server Room path at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup does not explicitly state ripd is running or that the 1.0.0.0/8 prefix is present on the CS->Server Room path—it only generically says routing/FRR looks correct.

The agent's observable claims (ICMP success, no TCP listeners, apache2 inactive) are well-supported by the investigation log, but the final diagnosis overreaches: it treats absent application services as a network fault without checking whether those services were expected to be running or whether the user reported application-level vs network-level failure. Thus grounding is strong, causality is only partly justified, and coverage misses the critical check that these services may be intentionally inactive.
